title: EXCLUSIVE: AI surveillance startup Flock Safety to cut several hundred jobs amid backlash, sources say
source_used: Reuters exclusive as relayed by CXO Digitalpulse (reuters.com returns 401; Tacoma News Tribune and marketscreener copies unreadable)
key_facts: Flock Safety plans to lay off about 270 employees, around 18% of its workforce of roughly 1,500, per a Reuters report of 9 Oct 2026.
The cuts follow a voluntary buyout (separation) programme announced in September; affected staff are expected to leave at the end of October.
Sources spoke anonymously because Flock has not publicly announced the layoffs; the company declined to comment.
Flock makes AI-powered surveillance cameras and software, including licence-plate readers; about 120,000 cameras in 49 US states.
It serves more than 4,800 law enforcement agencies and nearly 1,000 businesses.
A recent Reuters/Ipsos poll found 47% of Americans oppose Flock cameras in their communities and 38% support them.
It has raised more than $950 million; a March 2026 round of $275 million led by Andreessen Horowitz valued it at $7.5 billion.
It faces a Virginia privacy lawsuit alleging warrantless surveillance.
quote_evidence: Flock Safety, a US-based artificial intelligence surveillance startup, plans to lay off approximately 270 employees, representing around 18% of its workforce, as the company faces increasing opposition from communities and lawmakers over its surveillance technology.
The sources spoke on condition of anonymity because Flock Safety has not publicly announced the layoffs.
A recent Reuters/Ipsos poll found that 47% of Americans opposed the use of Flock cameras in their communities, while 38% supported their use.
why_it_matters_hint: A leading maker of police surveillance cameras is cutting about 18% of staff as opposition grows.
event_date: 9 Oct 2026 (people familiar spoke on Thursday 8 Oct)
notes: Reuters original blocked (401). Read a rewrite by CXO Digitalpulse that attributes everything to the Reuters report. Reuters headline says "several hundred"; the rewrite gives about 270 and 18%, also seen in the Investing.com headline "cut 18% of roles - Reuters".
